English: African marigold (Tagetes erecta) – mbangimwitu. Use against: bacteria, fungi, nematodes, insects (ants, beetles and many others). Preparation: crush 100-200g of the leaves, roots or flowers, pour on 1 litre of boiling water, stir, and soak for 24 hours, then add 1 litre of cold water. Spray on plants or into the soil.
Kiswahili: African marigold / Mbangimwitu (Tagetes erecta). Inazuia: bacteria, fungi, nematodes, wadudu (ants, beetles na wadudu wengine wengi). Kutayarisha: ponda gramu 100-200 ya matawi, mizizi na maua; mwaga kwa lita moja ya maji yaliyochemka; lowa kwa masaa ishirini na nne; ongeza lita moja ya maji baridi; nyunyiza kwa mimea au mchanga.
Source: https://infonet-biovision.org/tof-issue-no-17-septoct-2006-plant-extract-special-english-version (EN) / https://infonet-biovision.org/tof-issue-no-17-septoct-2006-plant-extract-special-swahili-version (SW)
Metadata: tone=advisory; platform=magazine; urgency=low; source_pair=true

English: Sweet potato (Ipomoea batatas) – kiazi kitamu. Use against: rice brown leaf spot, rice blast and other fungal diseases, insects (aphids). Preparation: crush and soak leaves in water, use as spray. Heavily starched water after cooking can be sprayed on small insects such as aphids.
Kiswahili: Sweet Potato / Kiazi kitamu (Ipomea batatas). Inazuia: rice brown leaf spot, rice blast na magonjwa mengine ya ukungu, wadudu (aphids). Kutayarisha: ponda na ulowe majani kwa maji, nyunyiza. Maji yanayo wanga mzito baada ya kupika yanaweza kunyunyizwa kwa wadudu wadogo kama aphids.
Source: https://infonet-biovision.org/tof-issue-no-17-septoct-2006-plant-extract-special-english-version (EN) / https://infonet-biovision.org/tof-issue-no-17-septoct-2006-plant-extract-special-swahili-version (SW)
Metadata: tone=advisory; platform=magazine; urgency=low; source_pair=true

English: Tea (Camellia sinensis) – chai. Use against: fungal diseases, insects, snails (woolly aphid, squash bug, termite mounds). Preparation: the used leaves can be spread around plants to repel snails. The liquid (tea), when cool, can be sprayed on plants.

English: When crops are damaged during or after harvest, they quickly spoil. You may not be able to sell your damaged produce, or you may be forced to sell at a reduced price. On the other hand, if you can reduce your losses, you can increase your income. At harvest time, when picking fruits, be careful not to knock them off the tree and onto the ground. If fruit falls, it gets bruised, disease and insects attack, and the fruit will quickly spoil. If you reduce the number of falls, you will have high quality produce to sell.
Kiswahili: Mazao yanapojeruhiwa wakati wa kuvuna au mara baada ya mavuno, yanaharibika kwa haraka. Unaweza kushindwa kuuza mazao yaliyoharibika au kujeruhiwa, na wakati mwingine ukalazimika kuyauza kwa bei ndogo. Kwa upande mwingine, kama utafanikiwa kupunguza hasara, unaweza pia kuongeza kipato chako. Wakati wa mavuno, unapokuwa ukichuma matunda, kuwa mwangalifu, usiyagonge kwenye mti au kuyaacha yakaanguka ardhini. Kama tunda likianguka chini, linaweza kupata michubuko, magonjwa na vijidudu vinalishambulia, na tunda huharibika. Kama utaweza kuzuia idadi ya matunda yanayoanguka chini, utakuwa na bidhaa bora sokoni.
Source: https://scripts.farmradio.fm/radio-script/avoid-post-harvest-losses-with-proper-handling/ (EN) / https://scripts.farmradio.fm/sw/mwongozo-wa-redio/epuka-hasara-baada-ya-mavuno-kwa-kutunza-mazao-yako-vizuri/ (SW) — Radio Spot #1 of 4, trimmed from full script

English: When crops are damaged during or after harvest, they quickly spoil, so you may be forced to sell at a reduced price. The best time to harvest fruits and vegetables is in the morning — wait until the dew has evaporated, then harvest before the day gets too hot. Harvesting later in the day leaves fruits and vegetables wilted or limp, with more disease and insect problems. Harvest in the morning for firmer, fresher produce.
Kiswahili: Matunda yanapokuwa yamejeruhiwa wakati wa kuvuna ama baada ya kuvuna, huharibika kwa haraka, hivyo unaweza kulazimika kuyauza kwa bei ya chini. Muda mzuri wa kuvuna matunda na mboga ni asubuhi — subiri mpaka umande umekauka, halafu vuna kabla jua halijawa kali. Ukivuna wakati wa jua kali, matunda na mboga zinaweza kusinyaa au kunyauka, na kushambuliwa zaidi na magonjwa au wadudu. Vuna asubuhi ili upate mazao mazuri na imara.
Source: https://scripts.farmradio.fm/radio-script/avoid-post-harvest-losses-with-proper-handling/ (EN) / https://scripts.farmradio.fm/sw/mwongozo-wa-redio/epuka-hasara-baada-ya-mavuno-kwa-kutunza-mazao-yako-vizuri/ (SW) — Radio Spot #2 of 4, trimmed from full script

English: It is wrong for farmers to apply any fertilizer without knowing what nutrients are lacking in the soil for the crop they intend to grow; farmers should seek advice from any KALRO station to have their soil tested.
Kiswahili: Ni makosa kwa wakulima kutumia mbolea yoyote bila kujua ni virutubisho gani vinavyokosekana kwenye udongo kwa zao wanalokusudia kulima; wakulima wanapaswa kutafuta ushauri kutoka kituo chochote cha KALRO ili kupima udongo wao.
Source: Farm Radio International / The Organic Farmer, TOF issue no. 156, May 2018 (infonet-biovision.org)

English: Farmers can increase millet and sorghum yields profitably by using fertilizer in combination with organic and natural techniques that conserve and concentrate soil moisture and organic matter.
Kiswahili: Wakulima wanaweza kuongeza mavuno ya mtama na uwele kwa faida kwa kutumia mbolea pamoja na mbinu za asili na kikaboni zinazohifadhi na kuongeza unyevu wa udongo na viumbe hai vya udongo.
Source: Farm Radio International / The Organic Farmer, TOF issue no. 32, January 2008 (infonet-biovision.org)

English: Farmers need access to information from research on how to farm sustainably, and indigenous knowledge should be prioritized in decisions that affect farmers.
Kiswahili: Wakulima wanahitaji kupata taarifa kutoka kwa utafiti kuhusu jinsi ya kulima kwa uendelevu, na maarifa asilia yanapaswa kupewa kipaumbele katika maamuzi yanayowaathiri wakulima.
Source: Farm Radio International / The Organic Farmer, TOF issue no. 211, April 2023 (infonet-biovision.org)

English: Using a smartphone app, farmers can get a diagnosis of a crop disease and recommendations on what treatment to apply.
Kiswahili: Kwa kutumia programu ya simu janja, wakulima wanaweza kupata utambuzi wa ugonjwa wa zao na mapendekezo ya matibabu ya kutumia.
Source: Farm Radio International / The Organic Farmer, TOF issue no. 227, June 2025 (infonet-biovision.org)

English: Although pyrethrum is quite poisonous when freshly harvested, it breaks down very quickly when exposed to the sun; after a few days there will be no poisonous compounds left and the produce will be safe to eat, though waiting one week is recommended to be absolutely sure.
Kiswahili: Ingawa pareto ni sumu kali inapovunwa ikiwa mbichi, huvunjika haraka sana inapopigwa na jua; baada ya siku chache hazitakuwa na kemikali za sumu zilizobaki na mazao yatakuwa salama kula, ingawa inashauriwa kusubiri wiki moja ili kuwa na uhakika kabisa.
Source: Farm Radio International / The Organic Farmer, TOF issue no. 77, October 2011 (infonet-biovision.org)

English: Remove honey that has stuck to the cloth using a spoon, and store the honey in a well-covered container.
Kiswahili: Ondoa asali inayoganda kwenye kitambaa kwa kutumia kijiko. Weka asali kwenye chombo kilichofunikwa vizuri.
Source: Mkulima Mbunifu (Biovision) issue no. 06, Mei 2012 (infonet-biovision.org)

English: If rains are predicted as normal to below normal, select drought-tolerant varieties of the crops recommended for your area, or change to drought-tolerant crops - for example, replacing maize with sorghum and millet.
Kiswahili: Ikiwa mvua zinatabiriwa kunyesha kiwango cha chini ya kiwango cha kawaida, chagua aina za mazao yanayostahimili ukame kwa eneo lako, au badilisha mazao na kupanda mazao yanayostahimili ukame. Kwa mfano, badala ya mahindi unaweza kupanda mtama au uwele.
Source: CGSpace/CCAFS-IITA "Climate smart agriculture: top ten decisions to make with weather info" poster - OCR-extracted 2026-07-15 with tesseract (eng/swa+eng), aligned by matching section headings between EN+SW versions (cgspace.cgiar.org items 62fd7239.../c4d42102...)
Metadata: tone=advisory; platform=poster; urgency=medium; source_pair=true; extraction=OCR

English: For rainfed agriculture, land should ideally be prepared at least two weeks before planting, with timing depending on when the rainy season is forecast to start, the crops being grown, and the topography.
Kiswahili: Kwa kilimo kinachotegemea mvua, shamba linapaswa kutayarishwa angalau wiki mbili kabla ya kupanda, kulingana na wakati msimu wa mvua unatarajiwa kuanza, zao litakalopandwa, na hali ya ardhi.
Source: CGSpace/CCAFS-IITA "Climate smart agriculture: top ten decisions to make with weather info" poster - OCR-extracted 2026-07-15 with tesseract (eng/swa+eng), aligned by matching section headings between EN+SW versions (cgspace.cgiar.org items 62fd7239.../c4d42102...)
Metadata: tone=advisory; platform=poster; urgency=medium; source_pair=true; extraction=OCR

English: If rains are predicted as normal, apply organic fertilizer one to two weeks before planting in bunds or by spreading, followed by shallow tillage; if rains are below normal, apply organic fertilizer two to three weeks before planting.
Kiswahili: Ikiwa mvua ni za kiwango cha kawaida, tumia mbolea ya asili wiki moja hadi mbili kabla ya kupanda kwenye malundo au kwa kusambaza kukifuatiwa na upaliliaji mwepesi; ikiwa mvua zinatabiriwa kunyesha chini ya kiwango cha kawaida, tumia mbolea ya asili wiki mbili hadi tatu kabla ya kupanda.
Source: CGSpace/CCAFS-IITA "Climate smart agriculture: top ten decisions to make with weather info" poster - OCR-extracted 2026-07-15 with tesseract (eng/swa+eng), aligned by matching section headings between EN+SW versions (cgspace.cgiar.org items 62fd7239.../c4d42102...)
Metadata: tone=advisory; platform=poster; urgency=medium; source_pair=true; extraction=OCR

English: Wait for the rains to start, and plant when the soil is moist enough - at least 20mm of rainfall over four consecutive days, or two days of heavy rain - or follow the advice from meteorology.
Kiswahili: Subiri hadi mvua zianze kunyesha, na panda wakati ardhi ina unyevu wa kutosha - angalau milimita 20 za mvua kwa siku nne mfululizo, au siku mbili za mvua kubwa - au fuata ushauri wa hali ya hewa.
Source: CGSpace/CCAFS-IITA "Climate smart agriculture: top ten decisions to make with weather info" poster - OCR-extracted 2026-07-15 with tesseract (eng/swa+eng), aligned by matching section headings between EN+SW versions (cgspace.cgiar.org items 62fd7239.../c4d42102...)
Metadata: tone=advisory; platform=poster; urgency=medium; source_pair=true; extraction=OCR

English: Weeding can be done manually or with herbicides; when using herbicides, use the correct product, wear the correct protective clothing, and follow correct disposal of containers. Weed more often when rains are heavy, and less often when rains are light.
Kiswahili: Palizi inaweza kufanywa kwa kutumia mikono au kwa dawa ya kuua magugu; wakati wa kutumia dawa za kuua magugu, tumia dawa inayofaa, vaa nguo sahihi za kujikinga, na uzingatie utupaji sahihi wa vyombo vya dawa baada ya kutumia. Wakati wa mvua nyingi, palilia magugu mara nyingi zaidi, na ikiwa mvua ni chache, punguza upaliliaji.
Source: CGSpace/CCAFS-IITA "Climate smart agriculture: top ten decisions to make with weather info" poster - OCR-extracted 2026-07-15 with tesseract (eng/swa+eng), aligned by matching section headings between EN+SW versions (cgspace.cgiar.org items 62fd7239.../c4d42102...)
Metadata: tone=advisory; platform=poster; urgency=medium; source_pair=true; extraction=OCR

English: For grains and legumes, harvest when the crop is completely dry; do not dry the harvest on bare soil, but spread a mat and store it in a dry, cool place. If rains are predicted, consider harvesting early and drying quickly.
Kiswahili: Kwa nafaka na mikunde, ni muhimu kuvuna wakati mazao yamekauka kabisa; usikaushe kwenye mchanga, bali tandaza mkeka na hifadhi mavuno katika sehemu kavu na baridi. Ikiwa mvua zinategemewa kunyesha, fikiria kuvuna mapema na kukausha haraka.
Source: CGSpace/CCAFS-IITA "Climate smart agriculture: top ten decisions to make with weather info" poster - OCR-extracted 2026-07-15 with tesseract (eng/swa+eng), aligned by matching section headings between EN+SW versions (cgspace.cgiar.org items 62fd7239.../c4d42102...)
Metadata: tone=advisory; platform=poster; urgency=medium; source_pair=true; extraction=OCR

English: Whenever possible, it is advised not to sell immediately after harvest when prices are low; harvest appropriately, store correctly, and sell when prices are higher.
Kiswahili: Inashauriwa, inapowezekana, kutouza mara tu baada ya mavuno wakati bei ziko chini; vuna ipasavyo, hifadhi vizuri, na uuze wakati bei ziko juu.
Source: CGSpace/CCAFS-IITA "Climate smart agriculture: top ten decisions to make with weather info" poster - OCR-extracted 2026-07-15 with tesseract (eng/swa+eng), aligned by matching section headings between EN+SW versions (cgspace.cgiar.org items 62fd7239.../c4d42102...)
Metadata: tone=advisory; platform=poster; urgency=medium; source_pair=true; extraction=OCR

English: Based on the seasonal rainfall forecast, adopt appropriate soil and water conservation measures: if rains are predicted above normal, focus on controlling erosion, protecting crops from flooding, and water harvesting; if below normal, focus on conserving soil moisture. If your land is sloping, add contour bunds to prevent soil erosion.
Kiswahili: Kulingana na utabiri wa msimu wa mvua, zingatia mbinu sahihi za kuhifadhi udongo na maji: ikiwa mvua zinatarajiwa kuwa nyingi kuliko kawaida, zingatia kudhibiti mmomonyoko wa udongo, kulinda mazao dhidi ya mafuriko, na kuvuna maji; ikiwa mvua zitakuwa chini ya kawaida, zingatia kuhifadhi unyevu wa udongo. Ikiwa ardhi yako iko mteremkoni, jenga matuta ili kuzuia mmomonyoko wa udongo.
Source: CGSpace/CCAFS-IITA "Climate smart agriculture: top ten decisions to make with weather info" poster - decision #2 (soil/water conservation), text-bundle extraction 2026-07-15 (not previously captured), aligned by matching section headings between EN+SW versions (cgspace.cgiar.org items 62fd7239.../c4d42102...)
Metadata: tone=advisory; platform=poster; urgency=medium; source_pair=true; extraction=text_bundle

English: Fertilizer can be organic, such as manure, or inorganic, or a mix of both; select the right fertilizer mix based on your soil, the crops you are growing, and the seasonal forecast.
Kiswahili: Mbolea inaweza kuwa ya asili, mfano samadi, au ya viwandani, au mchanganyiko wa aina zote mbili; chagua mchanganyiko sahihi wa mbolea kulingana na rutuba ya udongo wako, mazao unayopanda, na utabiri wa msimu.
Source: CGSpace/CCAFS-IITA "Climate smart agriculture: top ten decisions to make with weather info" poster - decision #4 (fertilizer type/mix selection), text-bundle extraction 2026-07-15 (not previously captured), aligned by matching section headings between EN+SW versions (cgspace.cgiar.org items 62fd7239.../c4d42102...)
Metadata: tone=advisory; platform=poster; urgency=medium; source_pair=true; extraction=text_bundle

English: Some pests and diseases occur when the weather is dry and others when there is heavy rain, so understand how the dynamics of major pests and diseases affecting your crops relate to the weather forecast, and identify which pesticides may be needed, where to obtain them, and how to use them correctly.
Kiswahili: Baadhi ya wadudu waharibifu na magonjwa hutokea wakati hali ya hewa ni kavu na wengine hutokea wakati kuna mvua nyingi, hivyo elewa jinsi mienendo ya wadudu na magonjwa makuu ya mazao yako inavyohusiana na utabiri wa hali ya hewa, kisha bainisha viuatilifu vinavyohitajika, mahali vinapopatikana, na jinsi ya kuvitumia kwa usahihi.
Source: CGSpace/CCAFS-IITA "Climate smart agriculture: top ten decisions to make with weather info" poster - decision #8 (pest/disease management), text-bundle extraction 2026-07-15 (not previously captured), aligned by matching section headings between EN+SW versions (cgspace.cgiar.org items 62fd7239.../c4d42102...)
Metadata: tone=advisory; platform=poster; urgency=medium; source_pair=true; extraction=text_bundle

English: To inoculate soybean seed, mix a sugar-water sticker solution, coat the seed evenly with it, then add the rhizobium inoculant and mix gently until every seed is covered; protect the inoculated seed from direct sunlight and keep it in the shade until you plant it.
Kiswahili: Ili kuweka bakteria (rhizobium) kwenye mbegu za soya, changanya myeyusho wa maji na sukari (kiambatanishi), paka kwenye mbegu kwa usawa, kisha ongeza dawa ya rhizobium na uchanganye kwa upole hadi kila mbegu ifunikwe; kinga mbegu zilizowekewa dawa dhidi ya jua moja kwa moja na uzitunze kivulini hadi wakati wa kupanda.
Source: CGSpace/N2Africa "Better soybean through good agricultural practices" leaflet, July 2014, For farmers in Ethiopia (CC-licensed) - Step 3: Inoculation excerpt, 2026-07-15 (cgspace.cgiar.org item 1c59e0c8-2fd5-4288-af93-7d585e4aea8a, handle 10568/76318)
Metadata: tone=advisory; platform=extension leaflet; urgency=low; translation=team; source_lang=en; country=Ethiopia

English: Common pests affecting soybean in Ethiopia are the African bollworm, cutworm, green stink bug, and aphid; leaf damage alone is unlikely to reduce yield and does not need spraying, but from flowering onwards soybean becomes attractive to pod-sucking bugs that can seriously reduce seed quality.
Kiswahili: Wadudu waharibifu wa kawaida wanaoshambulia soya nchini Ethiopia ni funza wa maharage ya Kiafrika, funza wa vipepeo, kunguni wa kijani, na vidukari; uharibifu wa majani pekee hauwezekani kupunguza mavuno na hauhitaji kunyunyizia dawa, lakini kuanzia kipindi cha maua, soya huvutia wadudu wanaonyonya mbegu ambao wanaweza kupunguza ubora wa mbegu kwa kiasi kikubwa.
Source: CGSpace/N2Africa "Better soybean through good agricultural practices" leaflet, July 2014, For farmers in Ethiopia (CC-licensed) - pest section excerpt, 2026-07-15 (cgspace.cgiar.org item 1c59e0c8-2fd5-4288-af93-7d585e4aea8a, handle 10568/76318)
Metadata: tone=advisory; platform=extension leaflet; urgency=low; translation=team; source_lang=en; country=Ethiopia

English: Climbing bean varieties yield more per unit of land than bush varieties but need staking for support; the highest yields come from stakes at least 175cm long, using at least 20,000 stakes per hectare, started two weeks after germination.
Kiswahili: Aina za maharagwe yanayopanda (yanayotambaa juu) hutoa mavuno mengi zaidi kwa eneo ukilinganisha na aina za kichaka, lakini yanahitaji kuwekewa mihimili ya kutegemeza; mavuno mazuri zaidi hupatikana kwa kutumia mihimili yenye urefu wa angalau sentimita 175, ikitumika angalau mihimili 20,000 kwa hekta, ikianza wiki mbili baada ya mbegu kuota.
Source: CGSpace/N2Africa "Better beans through good agricultural practices" leaflet, July 2014, For farmers in Ethiopia (CC-licensed) - staking climbing beans excerpt, 2026-07-15 (cgspace.cgiar.org item 3be2c6b5-0c6c-4078-b7c7-8edc90503d3a, handle 10568/76317)
Metadata: tone=advisory; platform=extension leaflet; urgency=low; translation=team; source_lang=en; country=Ethiopia

English: Bean stem maggot can be controlled through early planting, crop rotation, earthing up soil around the stem during weeding, using tolerant varieties, or treating seed with a systemic insecticide before planting.
Kiswahili: Funza wa shina la maharagwe anaweza kudhibitiwa kwa kupanda mapema, kubadilisha mazao (mzunguko wa mazao), kurundika udongo kuzunguka shina wakati wa kupalilia, kutumia aina zinazostahimili wadudu, au kutibu mbegu kwa dawa ya kuua wadudu inayoingia mmea kabla ya kupanda.
Source: CGSpace/N2Africa "Better beans through good agricultural practices" leaflet, July 2014, For farmers in Ethiopia (CC-licensed) - bean stem maggot control excerpt, 2026-07-15 (cgspace.cgiar.org item 3be2c6b5-0c6c-4078-b7c7-8edc90503d3a, handle 10568/76317)
Metadata: tone=advisory; platform=extension leaflet; urgency=low; translation=team; source_lang=en; country=Ethiopia

English: Rotate soybean with maize or sorghum for soil fertility benefits and disease control.
Kiswahili: Badilisha soya na mahindi au mtama ili kuimarisha rutuba ya udongo na kuzuia magonjwa.
Source: N2Africa "Best practices to maintain high yields and grain quality of soybean" checklist, for farmers in west Kenya - genuine EN+Swahili bilingual document (n2africa.org/sites/default/files/Best practice_soybean_English-Kiswahili.pdf)
Metadata: tone=advisory; platform=checklist; urgency=low; source_pair=true

English: Test the seeds for germination and plant only when germination is above 80%.
Kiswahili: Jaribu mbegu ya soya kama inamea kabla ya kupanda ili kuthibitisha kwamba asilimia zaidi ya 80 inamea.
Source: N2Africa "Best practices to maintain high yields and grain quality of soybean" checklist, for farmers in west Kenya - genuine EN+Swahili bilingual document (n2africa.org/sites/default/files/Best practice_soybean_English-Kiswahili.pdf)
Metadata: tone=advisory; platform=checklist; urgency=low; source_pair=true

English: Plant on time, when the soil is moist at the onset of the first rains; roots will not grow into dry soil and will not survive in water-logged soil.
Kiswahili: Panda kwa wakati ufaao, hakikisha mchanga una unyevu wa kutosha hasa wakati wa mvua za mwanzo. Mizizi ya soya haiwezi kustahimili mchanga mkavu ama mchanga wenye maji mengi.
Source: N2Africa "Best practices to maintain high yields and grain quality of soybean" checklist, for farmers in west Kenya - genuine EN+Swahili bilingual document (n2africa.org/sites/default/files/Best practice_soybean_English-Kiswahili.pdf)
Metadata: tone=advisory; platform=checklist; urgency=medium; source_pair=true

English: Spray recommended fungicide at recommended rates, first at flowering and once again as recommended, usually 21 days after the first spraying.
Kiswahili: Tumia dawa ya kuzuia magonjwa iliyopendekezwa, kwa kiwango kilichopendekezwa, wakati soya inapoanza kuweka maua. Rudia kunyunyizia dawa, kulingana na maagizo, kwa kawaida siku 21 baada ya kunyunyiza mara ya kwanza.
Source: N2Africa "Best practices to maintain high yields and grain quality of soybean" checklist, for farmers in west Kenya - genuine EN+Swahili bilingual document (n2africa.org/sites/default/files/Best practice_soybean_English-Kiswahili.pdf)
Metadata: tone=advisory; platform=checklist; urgency=medium; source_pair=true

English: Harvest early when 90-100% of pods are brown and dry, but before they become brittle and shatter.
Kiswahili: Vuna mapema wakati asilimia 90 hadi 100 ya mizoga imekauka na kubadilika kuwa rangi ya hudhurungi, lakini kabla haijaanza kupasuka.
Source: N2Africa "Best practices to maintain high yields and grain quality of soybean" checklist, for farmers in west Kenya - genuine EN+Swahili bilingual document (n2africa.org/sites/default/files/Best practice_soybean_English-Kiswahili.pdf)
Metadata: tone=advisory; platform=checklist; urgency=medium; source_pair=true

English: Clean the grain and dry it to a moisture content of 11-12%; soybeans above 13% moisture are likely to mould, and grain dried below 11% is likely to crack.
Kiswahili: Ondoa uchafu kwenye mbegu na ukaushe hadi unyevu ufike asilimia 11-12; soya zenye unyevu zaidi ya asilimia 13% huenda zikaoza, na ukikausha zaidi ya asilimia 11 mbegu zitapasuka.
Source: N2Africa "Best practices to maintain high yields and grain quality of soybean" checklist, for farmers in west Kenya - genuine EN+Swahili bilingual document (n2africa.org/sites/default/files/Best practice_soybean_English-Kiswahili.pdf)
Metadata: tone=advisory; platform=checklist; urgency=medium; source_pair=true

English: Store dry, clean grain only in clean bags - never recycled fertilizer, pesticide, or other chemical bags - and keep it in a cool, dry, ventilated place.
Kiswahili: Weka nafaka safi na iliyokauka kwenye magunia safi tu - usitumie magunia yaliyotumika kubeba mbolea, dawa za wadudu, au kemikali nyingine - na uhifadhi mahali penye ubaridi, ukavu, na hewa ya kutosha.
Source: N2Africa "Best practices to maintain high yields and grain quality of soybean" checklist, for farmers in west Kenya - genuine EN+Swahili bilingual document (n2africa.org/sites/default/files/Best practice_soybean_English-Kiswahili.pdf)
Metadata: tone=advisory; platform=checklist; urgency=low; source_pair=true

English: Harvest groundnuts only once fully mature; harvesting too early causes yield loss, while harvesting too late allows the groundnuts to become contaminated with aflatoxin.
Kiswahili: Vuna karanga wakati zimekomaa vizuri; kuvuna kabla ya wakati kunasababisha kupoteza mavuno, na kuchelewa kuvuna kunasababisha karanga kuingiwa na sumu kuvu (aflatoxin).
Source: Makutupora Agricultural Research Institute / N2Africa "Ongeza mavuno ya karanga kwa kutumia mbinu bora za kilimo" (Tanzania groundnut brochure) - Swahili-original, no English source exists (n2africa.org/sites/default/files/Groundnut Brochure, Tanzania.pdf)
Metadata: tone=advisory; platform=extension brochure; urgency=high; translation=team; source_lang=sw; country=Tanzania

English: Store well-dried groundnuts in clean bags in a clean, dry store free of moisture; where available, use a biological control product such as Aflasafe, following expert advice, to control aflatoxin contamination.
Kiswahili: Hifadhi karanga zilizokauka vizuri kwenye magunia safi na ghala safi, kavu na yasiyo na unyevu; tumia dawa ya kibaiolojia kama Aflasafe, ikiwa inapatikana, kwa kufuata ushauri wa wataalamu, ili kudhibiti sumu kuvu.
Source: Makutupora Agricultural Research Institute / N2Africa "Ongeza mavuno ya karanga kwa kutumia mbinu bora za kilimo" (Tanzania groundnut brochure) - Swahili-original, no English source exists (n2africa.org/sites/default/files/Groundnut Brochure, Tanzania.pdf)
Metadata: tone=advisory; platform=extension brochure; urgency=high; translation=team; source_lang=sw; country=Tanzania

English: Harvest cowpeas only once the pods are well dried; pick the pods individually, or uproot the whole plant once all the pods have dried.
Kiswahili: Kunde zivunwe wakati zimekauka vizuri; vuna kwa kuchuma vitumba au kung'oa mashina baada ya vitumba vyote kukauka.
Source: Ilonga Agricultural Research Institute / N2Africa "Lima kunde kwa lishe na kipato zaidi" (Tanzania cowpea brochure) - Swahili-original, no English source exists (n2africa.org/sites/default/files/Cowpea Brochure Tanzania.pdf)
Metadata: tone=advisory; platform=extension brochure; urgency=medium; translation=team; source_lang=sw; country=Tanzania

English: After harvesting, dry the cowpeas in the sun, thresh them with sticks, winnow, and dry again in the sun until fully dry; because cowpeas are quickly attacked by weevils, store them in special hermetic (PICS) storage bags.
Kiswahili: Baada ya kuvuna, anika kunde juani, zipige kwa fito, zipete, kisha zikaushe tena juani hadi zikauke vizuri; kwa kuwa kunde hushambuliwa haraka na wadudu, zihifadhi kwenye mifuko maalum (PICS bags).
Source: Ilonga Agricultural Research Institute / N2Africa "Lima kunde kwa lishe na kipato zaidi" (Tanzania cowpea brochure) - Swahili-original, no English source exists (n2africa.org/sites/default/files/Cowpea Brochure Tanzania.pdf)
Metadata: tone=advisory; platform=extension brochure; urgency=medium; translation=team; source_lang=sw; country=Tanzania

English: To treat vegetable seeds against disease before sowing, submerge them in water heated to the recommended temperature for the recommended time (for example, spinach, cabbage, pepper, tomato and eggplant: 50°C for 30 minutes; lettuce and celery: 47°C for 30 minutes), then cool the seeds immediately in clean water and dry them before sowing or storing.
Kiswahili: Ili kutibu mbegu za mboga dhidi ya magonjwa kabla ya kupanda, zamisha mbegu kwenye maji yaliyopashwa moto kwa kiwango na muda uliopendekezwa (kwa mfano, mchicha, kabichi, pilipili, nyanya na biringanya: nyuzi joto 50°C kwa dakika 30; saladi na seleri: nyuzi joto 47°C kwa dakika 30), kisha poza mbegu mara moja kwenye maji safi na uzikaushe kabla ya kupanda au kuzihifadhi.
Source: Farm Radio International / The Organic Farmer, TOF issue no. 40, September 2008 (infonet-biovision.org) - narrow-lexicon "recommendations" hit, previously scanned but not yet converted
Metadata: tone=advisory; platform=magazine; urgency=low; translation=team; source_lang=en; country=Kenya

English: When mixing urea into livestock feed, do not exceed 30% of the animal's digestible crude protein requirement from urea, as too much urea can overdose and harm the animal.
Kiswahili: Unapochanganya urea kwenye chakula cha mifugo, usizidishe asilimia 30 ya mahitaji ya protini mnyweka (digestible crude protein) ya mnyama kutoka kwa urea, kwa sababu urea nyingi kupita kiasi inaweza kumdhuru mnyama.
Source: Farm Radio International / The Organic Farmer, TOF issue no. 47, April 2009 (infonet-biovision.org) - narrow-lexicon "recommendations" hit, previously scanned but not yet converted
Metadata: tone=advisory; platform=magazine; urgency=medium; translation=team; source_lang=en; country=Kenya

English: To treat fodder tree seeds such as Leucaena using the hot-water method, pour plenty of boiling water over the seeds and stir gently for 2-5 minutes - do not soak too long, as hot water can kill the seeds - then pour off the hot water, replace it with cool water, and let the seeds soak for 12 hours until they swell visibly.
Kiswahili: Kutibu mbegu za miti ya malisho kama Leucaena kwa njia ya maji ya moto, mimina maji ya moto mengi juu ya mbegu na uzikoroge kwa upole kwa dakika 2-5 - usiziache muda mrefu kwa kuwa maji ya moto yanaweza kuua mbegu - kisha mwaga maji ya moto, badilisha na maji baridi, na uache mbegu ziloweke kwa masaa 12 hadi zivimbe wazi.
Source: Farm Radio International / The Organic Farmer, TOF issue no. 73, June 2011 (infonet-biovision.org) - narrow-lexicon "recommendations" hit, previously scanned but not yet converted
Metadata: tone=advisory; platform=magazine; urgency=low; translation=team; source_lang=en; country=Kenya

English: Before seasonal planning and planting, ask yourself: What do my soil test results say? Do I understand the recommendations and where I can source the recommended inputs? What inputs do I need to apply? Do I have a crop rotation calendar or plan? Better yields can only be achieved through proper soil management.
Kiswahili: Kabla ya kupanga na kupanda msimu, jiulize: Matokeo ya kipimo cha udongo wangu yanasema nini? Je, ninaelewa mapendekezo na wapi ninaweza kupata pembejeo zilizopendekezwa? Ni pembejeo gani ninahitaji kutumia? Je, nina ratiba au mpango wa mzunguko wa mazao? Mavuno bora yanaweza kupatikana tu kupitia usimamizi mzuri wa udongo.
Source: Farm Radio International / The Organic Farmer, TOF issue no. 169, August 2019 (infonet-biovision.org) - narrow-lexicon "recommendations" hit, previously scanned but not yet converted
Metadata: tone=advisory; platform=magazine; urgency=medium; translation=team; source_lang=en; country=Kenya

English: To control Tuta absoluta in tomatoes, begin control measures in the nursery and continue in the field: set out pheromone traps, or basins of water with a suspended attractant, at least one week before transplanting.
Kiswahili: Kudhibiti Tuta absoluta kwenye nyanya, anza hatua za udhibiti kitaluni na uendelee shambani: weka mitego ya homoni (pheromone), au mabeseni ya maji yenye kivutia kilichoning'inizwa, angalau wiki moja kabla ya kupandikiza miche.
Source: Farm Radio International / The Organic Farmer, TOF issue no. 190, May 2021 (infonet-biovision.org) - narrow-lexicon "recommendations" hit, previously scanned but not yet converted
Metadata: tone=advisory; platform=magazine; urgency=medium; translation=team; source_lang=en; country=Kenya

English: To achieve the optimal planting density for groundnut, sow one seed per hole at an inter-row spacing of 30cm and intra-row spacing of 15cm (or 45cm inter-row and 10cm intra-row for easier weeding); do the first weeding between 20 and 50 days after planting, depending on local weed growth.
Kiswahili: Ili kufikia msongamano bora wa upandaji wa karanga, panda mbegu moja kwa kila shimo kwa nafasi ya sentimita 30 kati ya mistari na sentimita 15 kati ya mimea (au sentimita 45 kati ya mistari na sentimita 10 kati ya mimea ili kurahisisha upaliliaji); fanya palizi ya kwanza kati ya siku 20 na 50 baada ya kupanda, kutegemea ukuaji wa magugu eneo lako.
Source: Africa RISING / IITA "Optimal spacing for groundnuts in smallholder farming systems" Technology Brief, March 2021, northern Ghana (CC-licensed) (cgspace.cgiar.org item 6e27f615-e5b9-4307-b4ff-2661f52f5c15)
Metadata: tone=advisory; platform=technology brief; urgency=low; translation=team; source_lang=en; country=Ghana

English: To minimize aflatoxin contamination in groundnut and maize and prevent losses, farmers can apply a biocontrol product called Aflasafe, which cuts aflatoxin levels by 96-100% down to safe levels for consumption, from the moment of harvest all the way through storage until the food is eaten.
Kiswahili: Ili kupunguza uchafuzi wa sumu kuvu (aflatoxin) kwenye karanga na mahindi na kuzuia hasara, wakulima wanaweza kutumia bidhaa ya kudhibiti kibaiolojia iitwayo Aflasafe, ambayo hupunguza viwango vya sumu kuvu kwa asilimia 96-100 hadi viwango salama vya kula, kuanzia mavuno hadi uhifadhi na hadi chakula kinapoliwa.
Source: Africa RISING / IITA "Optimal spacing for groundnuts in smallholder farming systems" Technology Brief, March 2021, northern Ghana (CC-licensed) (cgspace.cgiar.org item 6e27f615-e5b9-4307-b4ff-2661f52f5c15)
Metadata: tone=advisory; platform=technology brief; urgency=high; translation=team; source_lang=en; country=Ghana

English: Select a groundnut variety suited to your agro-ecological zone; in Nigeria, the Sahel, Sudan, and Northern and Southern Guinea savanna zones are the main groundnut-growing regions, so choose a variety adapted to your zone's maturity period and market preferences.
Kiswahili: Chagua aina ya karanga inayofaa kwa ukanda wako wa kiikolojia; nchini Nigeria, kanda za Sahel, Sudan, na savanna za Guinea ya Kaskazini na Kusini ndizo maeneo makuu ya kilimo cha karanga, hivyo chagua aina inayofaa kwa muda wa kukomaa na mahitaji ya soko ya eneo lako.
Source: N2Africa "Better groundnut through good agricultural practices" leaflet, For farmers in Nigeria (CC-licensed) - regional variety-selection excerpt, distinct from the shared template text (n2africa.org/sites/default/files/365 N2Africa Nigeria groundnut booklet.pdf)
Metadata: tone=advisory; platform=extension leaflet; urgency=low; translation=team; source_lang=en; country=Nigeria

English: Select a cowpea variety suited to your agro-ecological zone and cropping system; in Zimbabwe, Natural Regions IV and V (the drier regions) are suitable for growing cowpea, so consider maturity period, drought tolerance, and pest and disease resistance when choosing a variety.
Kiswahili: Chagua aina ya kunde inayofaa kwa ukanda wako wa kiikolojia na mfumo wa kilimo; nchini Zimbabwe, Kanda za Asili IV na V (maeneo makavu zaidi) yanafaa kwa kilimo cha kunde, hivyo zingatia muda wa kukomaa, ustahimilivu wa ukame, na uwezo wa kupambana na wadudu na magonjwa unapochagua aina.
Source: N2Africa "Better cowpea through good agricultural practices" leaflet, For farmers in Zimbabwe (CC-licensed) - regional variety-selection excerpt, distinct from the shared template text (n2africa.org/sites/default/files/290 N2Africa Zimbabwe cowpea booklet.pdf)
Metadata: tone=advisory; platform=extension leaflet; urgency=low; translation=team; source_lang=en; country=Zimbabwe

English: On hillsides, prepare a flat seedbed and control soil erosion, for example with terracing; on flat volcanic soils prone to flooding, prepare ridges about 75cm apart, since ridges help prevent the waterlogging that damages bean plants.
Kiswahili: Kwenye vilima, tayarisha kitalu tambarare na dhibiti mmomonyoko wa udongo, kwa mfano kwa kujenga matuta ya ngazi; kwenye udongo tambarare wa volkano unaokabiliwa na mafuriko, tayarisha matuta yenye nafasi ya sentimita 75 kati yao, kwani matuta husaidia kuzuia maji kujaa ambayo huharibu mimea ya maharagwe.
Source: N2Africa "Better beans through good agricultural practices" leaflet, For farmers in Rwanda (CC-licensed) - hillside/volcanic-soil land preparation excerpt, distinct from the shared template text (n2africa.org/sites/default/files/361 N2Africa Rwanda common beans booklet.pdf)
Metadata: tone=advisory; platform=extension leaflet; urgency=low; translation=team; source_lang=en; country=Rwanda

English: Farmers are advised to regularly monitor weather updates and follow guidance from agricultural extension officers to support timely decision-making and reduce weather-related risks.
Kiswahili: Wakulima wanashauriwa kufuatilia mara kwa mara taarifa za hali ya hewa na kuzingatia ushauri wa maafisa ugani wa kilimo ili kusaidia kufanya maamuzi kwa wakati na kupunguza hatari zinazohusiana na hali ya hewa.
Source: Kenya Meteorological Department (KMD) official advisory, 2026-05-23/24, quoted directly in "Kenya Met Issues Advisory to Farmers" (nairobileo.co.ke/news/article/27738/kenya-met-issues-advisory-to-farmers) - verified via independent web search while auditing NLP/Data/PSA_KE_Final.csv, not taken from that file (which has no Source column)
Metadata: tone=advisory; platform=news article quoting official advisory; urgency=medium; translation=team; source_lang=en; country=Kenya

English: To control aphids on beans, check the undersides of leaves on 20-30 plants across the field; if two or three plants have at least two groups of aphids, spray both sides of the leaves with soapy water in the early morning or evening.
Kiswahili: Kudhibiti vidukari kwenye maharagwe, kagua chini ya majani kwenye mimea 20-30 katika sehemu tofauti za shamba; ikiwa mimea miwili au mitatu ina angalau makundi mawili ya vidukari, nyunyizia pande zote za majani maji ya sabuni asubuhi mapema au jioni.
Source: CABI Plantwise "Factsheets for Farmers" - "Soap controls aphids in beans", Created in Kenya, September 2011, CC-licensed (factsheetadmin.plantwise.org/Uploads/PDFs/20117800545.pdf)
Metadata: tone=advisory; platform=CABI Plantwise factsheet; urgency=medium; translation=team; source_lang=en; country=Kenya

English: To manage black rot in brassica crops, rotate with non-Brassica plants and avoid replanting Brassica in the same field more than once every 2 years; control weeds around the farm, avoid overhead sprinkler irrigation, and plant only disease-free seeds or seedlings.
Kiswahili: Kudhibiti kuoza mweusi kwenye mazao ya jamii ya kabichi, badilisha mazao na mimea isiyo ya jamii ya kabichi na epuka kupanda kabichi kwenye shamba lile lile zaidi ya mara moja kila miaka 2; dhibiti magugu kuzunguka shamba, epuka umwagiliaji wa vinyunyizio juu, na panda mbegu au miche isiyo na ugonjwa pekee.
Source: CABI Plantwise "Factsheets for Farmers" - "Black rot on Brassica", Created in Kenya, December 2012, CC-licensed (factsheetadmin.plantwise.org/Uploads/PDFs/20137804264.pdf)
Metadata: tone=advisory; platform=CABI Plantwise factsheet; urgency=medium; translation=team; source_lang=en; country=Kenya

English: To mass-trap mango fruit flies, cut a plastic bottle in half, fill the lower half with fermented fruit juice, invert the top half as a funnel into it, and hang at least 10 traps per 100 square metres in the lower canopy of mango and guava trees - this only works if farmers in the area do it together.
Kiswahili: Kunasa nzi wa maembe kwa wingi, kata chupa ya plastiki katikati, jaza sehemu ya chini kwa maji ya matunda yaliyochachuka, geuza sehemu ya juu kama funeli ndani yake, kisha ning'iniza mitego angalau 10 kwa kila mita za mraba 100 kwenye sehemu ya chini ya miti ya maembe na mapera - hii hufanya kazi tu wakulima wa eneo hilo wakishirikiana.
Source: CABI Plantwise "Factsheets for Farmers" - "Come together to mass trap Mango fruit fly", Created in Tanzania, September 2012, CC-licensed (factsheetadmin.plantwise.org/Uploads/PDFs/20127802225.pdf)
Metadata: tone=advisory; platform=CABI Plantwise factsheet; urgency=medium; translation=team; source_lang=en; country=Tanzania

English: Wear protective equipment (overalls, boots, a mask covering the mouth and nose, a hard hat, goggles, and gloves) to protect yourself from the effects of pesticides. Do not use WHO Hazard Class I pesticides (red-label products) as they are very dangerous; also be careful with yellow-label products.
Kiswahili: Vaa zana za kujikinga (ovaroli, buti, kiziba mdomo na pua, kofia ngumu, miwani na glavu) kwa ajili ya kukukinga dhidi ya athari za viua wadudu. Usitumie viua wadudu vya Daraja la I kulingana na WHO (vyenye alama nyekundu) kwa sababu ni hatari sana; uwe mwangalifu pia na vyenye alama ya njano.
Source: CABI Plantwise "Vidokezo kwa Wakulima" (Tips for Farmers) - "Upuliziaji salama kwa kutumia bomba la kupulizia kiua wadudu" (Safe spraying using a pesticide sprayer), Created in Tanzania, September 2013, CC-licensed, Kiswahili-original (factsheetadmin.plantwise.org/Uploads/PDFs/20147801018.pdf)
Metadata: tone=advisory; platform=CABI Plantwise factsheet; urgency=high; translation=team; source_lang=sw; country=Tanzania

English: To prevent mealybug spread in cassava, collect planting cuttings from a known mealybug-free area (not during the dry season), cut off the top and bottom 10-20cm of each stem, then soak the remaining cuttings in hot (not boiling) water for 5 minutes before cooling and planting.
Kiswahili: Ili kuzuia kuenea kwa vidung'ata kwenye muhogo, chukua vipandikizi kutoka eneo linalojulikana kutokuwa na vidung'ata (si wakati wa kiangazi), kata sentimita 10-20 za juu na chini za kila shina, kisha loweka vipandikizi vilivyobaki kwenye maji ya moto (yasiyochemka) kwa dakika 5 kabla ya kupoza na kupanda.
Source: CABI Plantwise "Factsheets for Farmers" - "Clean cassava cuttings to stop mealybug spread", Created in Tanzania, September 2013, CC-licensed (factsheetadmin.plantwise.org/Uploads/PDFs/20147801029.pdf)
Metadata: tone=advisory; platform=CABI Plantwise factsheet; urgency=medium; translation=team; source_lang=en; country=Tanzania

English: Inspect your maize field often while plants are young; uproot infected plants as soon as they show disease signs and put the whole plant in a sack so leafhoppers do not spread to healthy plants, then plant a resistant maize variety next season.
Kiswahili: Kagua shamba lako la mahindi mara kwa mara wakati mimea bado michanga; ng'oa mimea iliyoathirika mara tu inapoonyesha dalili za ugonjwa na uiweke kwenye gunia ili wadudu wasieneze ugonjwa kwenye mimea yenye afya, kisha panda aina ya mahindi inayostahimili ugonjwa msimu ujao.
Source: CABI Plantwise "Factsheets for Farmers" - "Maize streak virus", Created in Kenya, September 2011, CC-BY-SA 4.0 (factsheetadmin.plantwise.org/Uploads/PDFs/20117800551.pdf)
Metadata: tone=advisory; platform=CABI Plantwise factsheet; urgency=medium; translation=team; source_lang=en; country=Kenya

English: To manage Tomato Yellow Leaf Curl Virus, remove and burn diseased plants, plant resistant varieties, intercrop with maize to reduce whitefly access to the crop, and control whiteflies with oil sprays or insecticides while always wearing protective clothing and following the product label.
Kiswahili: Kudhibiti Virusi vya Ukunjaji Manjano wa Majani ya Nyanya (TYLCV), ondoa na uchome mimea iliyoathirika, panda aina zinazostahimili ugonjwa, changanya na mahindi ili kupunguza uwezo wa inzi weupe kufikia zao, na dhibiti inzi weupe kwa dawa za mafuta au viua wadudu huku ukivaa nguo za kujikinga na kufuata maelekezo kwenye lebo ya bidhaa.
Source: CABI Plantwise "Factsheets for Farmers" - "Tomato Yellow Leaf Curl Virus on Tomato", Created in Kenya, December 2012, CC-licensed (factsheetadmin.plantwise.org/Uploads/PDFs/20137804221.pdf)
Metadata: tone=advisory; platform=CABI Plantwise factsheet; urgency=medium; translation=team; source_lang=en; country=Kenya

English: During hot weather, protect farm animals from heat stress by providing well-ventilated shelter and plenty of cool drinking water; do not move animals between 10:00am and 4:00pm, the hottest part of the day.
Kiswahili: Wakati wa hali ya hewa ya joto, kinga wanyama wa shambani dhidi ya mkazo wa joto kwa kuwapa banda lenye mzunguko mzuri wa hewa na maji ya kunywa yenye ubaridi wa kutosha; usiwahamishe wanyama kati ya saa 10:00 asubuhi na saa 4:00 mchana, wakati wa joto kali zaidi.
Source: NAERLS (Nigerian Livestock Early Warning System), Climate Factsheet No. 003, 1 May 2024 (naerls.gov.ng/wp-content/uploads/2024/04/N-LEWS-Climate-factsheet-May.pdf)
Metadata: tone=advisory; platform=government factsheet; urgency=medium; translation=team; source_lang=en; country=Nigeria

English: Feed poultry and swine during the cooler hours of early morning and late evening, and cool large livestock such as cattle, sheep, goats, and pigs by misting them with water or letting them wallow in shallow water.
Kiswahili: Lisha kuku na nguruwe wakati wa saa za baridi za asubuhi na jioni, na saidia kupoza mifugo mikubwa kama ng'ombe, kondoo, mbuzi, na nguruwe kwa kuwanyunyizia maji au kuwaruhusu kulala kwenye maji machache.
Source: NAERLS (Nigerian Livestock Early Warning System), Climate Factsheet No. 003, 1 May 2024 (naerls.gov.ng/wp-content/uploads/2024/04/N-LEWS-Climate-factsheet-May.pdf)
Metadata: tone=advisory; platform=government factsheet; urgency=medium; translation=team; source_lang=en; country=Nigeria

English: In fish farms, manage high water temperatures by exchanging at least 10-20% of pond water daily with cooler water, aerating the water, maintaining pond depth of at least 1-1.5m, shading ponds from direct sun, and reducing fish stocking density during hot weather.
Kiswahili: Katika mabwawa ya samaki, punguza joto kali la maji kwa kubadilisha angalau asilimia 10-20 ya maji ya bwawa kila siku kwa maji baridi zaidi, kuweka hewa ndani ya maji, kudumisha kina cha bwawa cha angalau mita 1-1.5, kuweka kivuli juu ya mabwawa dhidi ya jua moja kwa moja, na kupunguza idadi ya samaki wakati wa hali ya hewa ya joto.
Source: NAERLS (Nigerian Livestock Early Warning System), Climate Factsheet No. 003, 1 May 2024 (naerls.gov.ng/wp-content/uploads/2024/04/N-LEWS-Climate-factsheet-May.pdf)
Metadata: tone=advisory; platform=government factsheet; urgency=medium; translation=team; source_lang=en; country=Nigeria

English: Livestock farmers and feed millers across Nigeria can lower input costs by planting maize, sorghum, groundnuts, and cowpeas at the start of the rainy season to use as animal feed and feed ingredients.
Kiswahili: Wafugaji na wasindikaji wa vyakula vya mifugo nchini Nigeria wanaweza kupunguza gharama za malighafi kwa kupanda mahindi, mtama, karanga, na kunde mwanzoni mwa msimu wa mvua kwa ajili ya chakula cha mifugo na malighafi zake.
Source: NAERLS (Nigerian Livestock Early Warning System), Climate Factsheet No. 004, 5 June 2024 (naerls.gov.ng/wp-content/uploads/2024/06/N-LEWS-Climate-factsheet-June.pdf)
Metadata: tone=advisory; platform=government factsheet; urgency=low; translation=team; source_lang=en; country=Nigeria

English: To prevent Fall Armyworm infestation, use high-quality, disease-free seed, avoid late or staggered planting, and increase plant diversity in your plots (for example intercropping) to make maize less attractive to armyworm moths.
Kiswahili: Ili kuzuia mashambulizi ya viwavi jeshi, tumia mbegu bora zisizo na magonjwa, epuka kupanda kuchelewa au kwa nyakati tofauti, na ongeza aina mbalimbali za mimea shambani (kwa mfano kilimo mseto) ili kufanya mahindi yasiwe ya kuvutia kwa nondo wa viwavi jeshi.
Source: FAO, "How to Manage Fall Armyworm: A Quick Guide for Smallholders" (FAW Guidance Note 4), CA0435EN/1/07.18 (openknowledge.fao.org/server/api/core/bitstreams/359d03ae-27c3-4257-a906-a4e155c2a2b1/content)
Metadata: tone=advisory; platform=FAO technical guidance note; urgency=medium; translation=team; source_lang=en

English: Starting one week after planting, walk through your maize field every 3-4 days to check plant health and look for Fall Armyworm egg masses, young larvae, and leaf damage, so problems can be caught and treated early.
Kiswahili: Kuanzia wiki moja baada ya kupanda, tembea shambani kila baada ya siku 3-4 kukagua afya ya mimea na kutafuta mayai ya viwavi jeshi, viwavi wachanga, na uharibifu wa majani, ili matatizo yagundulike na kushughulikiwa mapema.
Source: FAO, "How to Manage Fall Armyworm: A Quick Guide for Smallholders" (FAW Guidance Note 4), CA0435EN/1/07.18 (openknowledge.fao.org/server/api/core/bitstreams/359d03ae-27c3-4257-a906-a4e155c2a2b1/content)
Metadata: tone=advisory; platform=FAO technical guidance note; urgency=medium; translation=team; source_lang=en

English: Control Fall Armyworm by crushing egg masses and picking off young larvae by hand before they enter the maize whorl; avoid unnecessary chemical pesticide use, which is costly and can kill the natural predators that help control the pest.
Kiswahili: Dhibiti viwavi jeshi kwa kuponda mayai na kuokota viwavi wachanga kwa mkono kabla hawajaingia ndani ya kitovu cha mmea wa mahindi; epuka matumizi yasiyo ya lazima ya dawa za kuulia wadudu, kwani ni ghali na yanaweza kuua wadudu waharibifu wa asili wanaosaidia kudhibiti viwavi jeshi.
Source: FAO, "How to Manage Fall Armyworm: A Quick Guide for Smallholders" (FAW Guidance Note 4), CA0435EN/1/07.18 (openknowledge.fao.org/server/api/core/bitstreams/359d03ae-27c3-4257-a906-a4e155c2a2b1/content)
Metadata: tone=advisory; platform=FAO technical guidance note; urgency=medium; translation=team; source_lang=en

English: To manage tomato wilt (kiwotoka), rotate tomatoes with maize, beans, or sweet potatoes for several years, plant tomatoes in a different plot each year, try different varieties to find resistant ones, and pull up and burn any wilting plant you find.
Kiswahili: Ili kudhibiti ugonjwa wa mnyauko wa nyanya (kiwotoka), badilisha mazao kwa kupanda mahindi, maharage, au viazi vitamu kwa miaka kadhaa badala ya nyanya, panda nyanya sehemu tofauti kila mwaka, jaribu aina tofauti za nyanya kutafuta zinazostahimili ugonjwa, na ung'oe na kuchoma mmea wowote unaonyauka.
Source: CABI Plantwise, "Tomato wilt or kiwotoka" Factsheet for Farmers, Created in Uganda, July 2006 (factsheetadmin.plantwise.org/Uploads/PDFs/20103326447.pdf), CC-BY-SA 4.0
Metadata: tone=advisory; platform=CABI Plantwise factsheet; urgency=medium; translation=team; source_lang=en; country=Uganda

English: To control tomato red spider mite, avoid continuous tomato cropping, remove and destroy crop residues before replanting, wash and sun-dry stakes and twine before reuse, inspect crop borders regularly, and spray water on plants to reduce the dust that mites thrive in.
Kiswahili: Ili kudhibiti utitiri mwekundu wa nyanya, epuka kupanda nyanya mfululizo shambani hilo hilo, ondoa na uteketeze mabaki ya mazao kabla ya kupanda upya, osha na kaushia jua vigingi na kamba kabla ya kuzitumia tena, kagua mipaka ya shamba mara kwa mara, na nyunyizia maji juu ya mimea ili kupunguza vumbi linalopendelewa na utitiri.
Source: CABI Plantwise, "Tomato red spider mite" Factsheet for Farmers, Created in Kenya, October 2012 (factsheetadmin.plantwise.org/Uploads/PDFs/20137804187.pdf), CC-BY-SA 4.0
Metadata: tone=advisory; platform=CABI Plantwise factsheet; urgency=medium; translation=team; source_lang=en; country=Kenya

English: To manage potato bacterial wilt, uproot and remove infected plants from the field, buy certified disease-free seed potatoes, rotate potatoes/tomatoes/peppers/eggplants with maize, bananas, beans, cassava, or millet, remove all volunteer potato tubers after harvest, and keep field tools clean.
Kiswahili: Ili kudhibiti mnyauko bakteria wa viazi, ng'oa na uondoe mimea iliyoathirika shambani, nunua mbegu za viazi zisizo na magonjwa zilizothibitishwa, badilisha mazao kwa kupanda mahindi, migomba, maharage, muhogo, au ulezi badala ya viazi, nyanya, pilipili hoho au biringanya, ondoa viazi vyote vilivyobaki shambani baada ya mavuno, na tumia zana safi shambani.
Source: CABI Plantwise "Factsheets for Farmers" - "Potato bacteria wilt", Created in Rwanda, May 2012, CC-BY-SA 4.0 (factsheetadmin.plantwise.org/Uploads/PDFs/20127801777.pdf)
Metadata: tone=advisory; platform=CABI Plantwise factsheet; urgency=medium; translation=team; source_lang=en; country=Rwanda

English: To reduce Brown Leaf Spot in cassava, use good, healthy planting stock, destroy infected crop husks after harvest, and plant early so the crop grows vigorously; if healthy planting material isn't available, dip cassava stems in a diluted fungicide before planting.
Kiswahili: Ili kupunguza ugonjwa wa Brown Leaf Spot kwenye muhogo, tumia vipando bora na vyenye afya, teketeza mabaki ya mimea iliyoathirika baada ya mavuno, na panda mapema ili zao likue vizuri; iwapo vipando vyenye afya havipatikani, chovya mashina ya muhogo kwenye myeyusho hafifu wa dawa ya kuvu kabla ya kupanda.
Source: CABI Plantwise "Factsheets for Farmers" - "Brown Leaf Spot (BLS) of Cassava", Created in Uganda, August 2012, CC-BY-SA 4.0 (factsheetadmin.plantwise.org/Uploads/PDFs/20137804388.pdf)
Metadata: tone=advisory; platform=CABI Plantwise factsheet; urgency=medium; translation=team; source_lang=en; country=Uganda

English: To free cassava cuttings of mealybugs before planting, heat water until it is too hot to hold a finger in for more than five seconds (about 60C), then dip the cuttings in this hot water for one minute only - do not soak longer, as this can kill the cuttings too.
Kiswahili: Ili kuondoa utitiri wa muhogo kwenye vipando kabla ya kupanda, pasha maji moto hadi yasishikike na kidole kwa zaidi ya sekunde tano (karibu nyuzi joto 60), kisha chovya vipando kwenye maji hayo moto kwa dakika moja tu - usiviache muda mrefu zaidi, kwani vinaweza kufa navyo.
Source: CABI Plantwise "Factsheets for Farmers" - "Warm water treatment of cassava mealybug", Created in Zambia, August 2013, CC-BY-SA 4.0 (factsheetadmin.plantwise.org/Uploads/PDFs/20147801347.pdf)
Metadata: tone=advisory; platform=CABI Plantwise factsheet; urgency=medium; translation=team; source_lang=en; country=Zambia

English: To control cassava mosaic disease, check plants weekly for the first 2-3 months after planting; when you find diseased plants, uproot them by hand once a week, replace them immediately with healthy cuttings, and burn the uprooted diseased plants after sun-drying them away from the field.
Kiswahili: Ili kudhibiti ugonjwa wa batobato ya muhogo, kagua mimea kila wiki kwa miezi 2-3 ya kwanza baada ya kupanda; ukikuta mimea iliyoathirika, ing'oe kwa mkono mara moja kwa wiki, badilisha papo hapo na vipando vyenye afya, na choma mimea iliyong'olewa baada ya kuikausha juani mbali na shamba.
Source: CABI Plantwise "Factsheets for Farmers" - "Control of cassava mosaic disease by uprooting", Created in Tanzania, October 2014, CC-BY-SA 4.0 (factsheetadmin.plantwise.org/Uploads/PDFs/20157800492.pdf)
Metadata: tone=advisory; platform=CABI Plantwise factsheet; urgency=medium; translation=team; source_lang=en; country=Tanzania

English: To trap snails away from your vegetables, place piles of fresh pawpaw leaves or cassava peels (about the size of a football) near your plots in the evening, about half a metre to a metre from the plants; collect and destroy the snails gathered on the traps early the next morning.
Kiswahili: Ili kunasa konokono mbali na mboga zako, weka lundo la majani mabichi ya papai au maganda ya muhogo (kwa ukubwa wa mpira wa miguu) karibu na shamba jioni, umbali wa nusu mita hadi mita moja kutoka kwa mimea; kusanya na uangamize konokono waliokusanyika kwenye mtego asubuhi na mapema.
Source: CABI Plantwise "Factsheets for Farmers" - "Pawpaw leaves and cassava peels to trap snails", Created in Zambia, December 2014, CC-BY-SA 4.0 (factsheetadmin.plantwise.org/Uploads/PDFs/20167800153.pdf)
Metadata: tone=advisory; platform=CABI Plantwise factsheet; urgency=low; translation=team; source_lang=en; country=Zambia

English: To manage mango bacterial black spot, plant tolerant varieties such as Heidi or Sensation, plant windbreaks to reduce rain splash, burn infected fruits and dead branches, prune to improve airflow and light in the canopy, and apply copper sprays or fungicides regularly.
Kiswahili: Ili kudhibiti ugonjwa wa madoa meusi ya bakteria kwenye maembe, panda aina zinazostahimili kama Heidi au Sensation, panda vizuia upepo kupunguza kunyunyizwa kwa mvua, choma matunda yaliyoathirika na matawi yaliyokufa, katakata matawi ili kuboresha mzunguko wa hewa na mwanga, na nyunyizia dawa za shaba au za kuvu mara kwa mara.
Source: CABI Plantwise "Factsheets for Farmers" - "Mango Bacterial Black Spot", Created in Uganda, August 2012, CC-BY-SA 4.0 (factsheetadmin.plantwise.org/Uploads/PDFs/20137804392.pdf)
Metadata: tone=advisory; platform=CABI Plantwise factsheet; urgency=medium; translation=team; source_lang=en; country=Uganda

English: When using legume seed inoculant: use the correct inoculant for each legume species and check the expiration date; protect it from sun and heat, storing between 4-26C; and keep it in tightly closed bags, removing it only with clean utensils.
Kiswahili: Unapotumia chanjo ya mbegu za mikunde: tumia chanjo ifaayo kwa kila aina ya mikunde na angalia muda wa kuharibika; kinga chanjo kutoka kwa jua na joto, ihifadhi kwa joto la 4-26C; na iweke kwenye mkoba uliofungwa kikamilifu, ukiondoa kwa chombo kisafi tu.
Source: N2Africa, "Biological Nitrogen Fixation and Grain Legume Enterprise: Guidelines for N2Africa Master Farmers" (CIAT-TSBF/FORMAT, 2010) - English (n2africa.org/sites/default/files/Master%20farmer%20guidelines_BNF%20-%20GL%20enterprise%20s_0.pdf) + Kiswahili edition (n2africa.org/sites/default/files/Master%20farmer%20guidelines_BNF-GL_Kiswahili%20version%20incl%20cover-S_0.pdf), "Utumizi bora wa chanjo cha mikunde" checklist
Metadata: tone=advisory; platform=extension guideline booklet; urgency=medium

English: When inoculating legume seeds: use a sticker such as gum arabic to bind the inoculant to the seed (smaller seeds need more sticker), use no less than 10g of inoculant per kg of seed, and inoculate just before planting, covering the seed with soil soon after to protect it from sun and drying.
Kiswahili: Unapochanja mbegu za mikunde: tumia gamu kama Gum Arabic kushikisha chanjo kwenye mbegu (mbegu ndogo huitaji gamu nyingi), tumia chanjo isiyopungua gramu 10 kwa kilo ya mbegu, na chanja mbegu kabla tu ya kupanda, ukizifunika mchangani mara tu baada ya kupanda kuzikinga na jua na kukauka.
Source: N2Africa, "Biological Nitrogen Fixation and Grain Legume Enterprise: Guidelines for N2Africa Master Farmers" (CIAT-TSBF/FORMAT, 2010) - English (n2africa.org/sites/default/files/Master%20farmer%20guidelines_BNF%20-%20GL%20enterprise%20s_0.pdf) + Kiswahili edition (n2africa.org/sites/default/files/Master%20farmer%20guidelines_BNF-GL_Kiswahili%20version%20incl%20cover-S_0.pdf), "Utumizi bora wa chanjo cha mikunde" checklist
Metadata: tone=advisory; platform=extension guideline booklet; urgency=medium

English: When harvesting and drying groundnuts, do not harvest in the rain or pile the pods into heaps that stay damp, since this encourages mould and dangerous aflatoxin contamination; handle pods carefully to avoid splitting the seeds, which lowers their sale value.
Kiswahili: Wakati wa kuvuna na kukausha karanga, usivune wakati wa mvua au kurundika maganda kwenye lundo linalobaki na unyevu, kwani hii huchochea ukungu na sumu hatari ya aflatoxin; shughulikia maganda kwa uangalifu ili kuepuka kupasuka kwa mbegu, jambo linalopunguza thamani yake ya soko.
Source: N2Africa Outreach Project, "Grain Legume Processing Handbook: Value Addition to Bean, Cowpea, Groundnut and Soybean by Small-Scale African Farmers" (Woomer et al.) (n2africa.org/sites/default/files/Handbook%20Grain%20Legume%20Processing%20S_0.pdf)
Metadata: tone=advisory; platform=extension handbook; urgency=high; translation=team; source_lang=en

English: As part of Zambia's national drought response, farming households in affected areas are being provided with seeds and planting materials for early-maturing, drought-resistant crops (including vegetables, maize, mixed beans, and cowpeas), and encouraged to diversify crops to reduce reliance on staples and improve dietary diversity.
Kiswahili: Kama sehemu ya mpango wa kitaifa wa kukabiliana na ukame nchini Zambia, kaya za wakulima katika maeneo yaliyoathirika zinapatiwa mbegu na vipando vya mazao yanayokomaa mapema na yanayostahimili ukame (ikiwemo mboga, mahindi, maharagwe mchanganyiko, na kunde), na kuhimizwa kubadilisha mazao ili kupunguza utegemezi wa chakula kimoja na kuboresha mlo mchanganyiko.
Source: Zambia Drought Response Appeal (May-December 2024), Agriculture sector response strategy, co-led by WFP/FAO with the Zambian government's DMMU-coordinated national drought response (unocha.org/attachments/9890d85b-000f-4eb3-81cf-7e0984a452ea/Zambia%20Drought%20Response%20Appeal%20_06052024%20FINAL%20V2.pdf)
Metadata: tone=advisory; platform=government/UN drought response appeal; urgency=high; translation=team; source_lang=en; country=Zambia

English: As part of Zambia's national drought response, affected agro-pastoral communities are receiving livestock disease surveillance and management support, supplementary animal feed, and rehabilitated dams, boreholes, and weirs to secure water access for irrigation and livestock.
Kiswahili: Kama sehemu ya mpango wa kitaifa wa kukabiliana na ukame nchini Zambia, jamii za wafugaji-wakulima walioathirika zinapokea usaidizi wa ufuatiliaji na udhibiti wa magonjwa ya mifugo, chakula cha ziada cha mifugo, na ukarabati wa mabwawa, visima, na mabwawa madogo ili kuhakikisha upatikanaji wa maji kwa umwagiliaji na mifugo.
Source: Zambia Drought Response Appeal (May-December 2024), Agriculture sector response strategy, co-led by WFP/FAO with the Zambian government's DMMU-coordinated national drought response (unocha.org/attachments/9890d85b-000f-4eb3-81cf-7e0984a452ea/Zambia%20Drought%20Response%20Appeal%20_06052024%20FINAL%20V2.pdf)
Metadata: tone=advisory; platform=government/UN drought response appeal; urgency=high; translation=team; source_lang=en; country=Zambia

English: When practicing companion planting, choose crops carefully: for example, intercrop maize with legumes since beans fix nitrogen that maize needs, but avoid pairing two 'heavy feeder' crops like maize and sunflower that compete heavily for the same nutrients.
Kiswahili: Unapofanya kilimo mseto, chagua mazao kwa uangalifu: kwa mfano, changanya mahindi na mikunde kwani maharagwe huweka naitrojeni ambayo mahindi huhitaji, lakini epuka kuchanganya mazao mawili 'yanayohitaji virutubisho vingi' kama mahindi na alizeti ambayo hushindania virutubisho sawa.
Source: Farm Radio International, "Backgrounder: Benefits of crop companion planting and mutualism" (scripts.farmradio.fm/radio-script/backgrounder-benefits-crop-companion-planting-mutualism/, Swahili: scripts.farmradio.fm/sw/mwongozo-wa-redio/taarifa-za-awali-faida-za-upandaji-wa-mazao-mbalimbali-kwa-njia-ya-mseto/)
Metadata: tone=advisory; platform=Farm Radio International backgrounder

English: To maintain healthy soil in conservation agriculture, cover at least 30% of your land with crop residues or cover crops; this reduces weeds, prevents erosion of fertile topsoil, and conserves soil moisture, especially in dry regions. Leguminous cover crops like mucuna, sun hemp, and lablab beans can also cut chemical fertilizer use by 60-80% without lowering yields.
Kiswahili: Ili kutunza udongo vizuri katika kilimo hifadhi, funika angalau asilimia 30 ya shamba lako kwa mabaki ya mazao au mazao funika; hii hupunguza magugu, huzuia mmomonyoko wa udongo wenye rutuba, na kuhifadhi unyevu wa udongo, hasa katika maeneo yenye ukame. Mazao funika ya jamii ya mikunde kama mukuna, sunhemp, na lablab pia yanaweza kupunguza matumizi ya mbolea za kemikali kwa asilimia 60-80 bila kupunguza mavuno.
Source: Farm Radio International, "Backgrounder: Using permanent soil cover in conservation agriculture" (scripts.farmradio.fm/radio-script/backgrounder-using-permanent-soil-cover-conservation-agriculture/, Swahili: scripts.farmradio.fm/sw/mwongozo-wa-redio/utangulizi-utumiaji-wa-mazao-funika-kwenye-kilimo-hifadhi/)
Metadata: tone=advisory; platform=Farm Radio International backgrounder

English: To dry rice seed without spoiling it, build a simple raised table from wood or bamboo instead of drying on the ground; air moves freely under the seed so it dries faster and stays clean, and the table can be quickly carried indoors when it rains.
Kiswahili: Ili kukausha mbegu za mpunga bila kuharibika, tengeneza meza rahisi ya mbao au mianzi badala ya kukausha ardhini; hewa hupita kwa urahisi chini ya mbegu hivyo hukauka haraka na kubaki safi, na meza inaweza kubebwa ndani haraka wakati wa mvua.
Source: Farm Radio International, "Dry rice seed off the ground to ensure top quality" (scripts.farmradio.fm/radio-script/dry-rice-seed-off-the-ground-to-ensure-top-quality/)
Metadata: tone=advisory; platform=Farm Radio International script; urgency=low; translation=team; source_lang=en

English: To manage cassava mosaic disease: plant only cuttings showing no signs of infection, taken from a clean disease-free field; uproot and bury any plant that develops symptoms as soon as you see them; plant tolerant varieties (in Malawi: Sauti, Sagonja, Yizaso, Chamandanda); and rotate crops to prevent the disease building up in the soil.
Kiswahili: Ili kudhibiti ugonjwa wa batobato ya muhogo: panda vipando visivyoonyesha dalili za maambukizi tu, vilivyotoka shamba safi lisilo na ugonjwa; ng'oa na uzike mmea wowote unaoonyesha dalili mara utakapouona; panda aina zinazostahimili (nchini Malawi: Sauti, Sagonja, Yizaso, Chamandanda); na badilisha mazao ili kuzuia ugonjwa kujengeka udongoni.
Source: Farm Radio International, "One head cannot lift a roof (Mutu umodzi susenza denga)" (scripts.farmradio.fm/radio-script/one-head-cannot-lift-a-roof-mutu-umodzi-susenza-denga/), Malawi cassava mosaic disease drama
Metadata: tone=advisory; platform=Farm Radio International script; urgency=medium; translation=team; source_lang=en; country=Malawi

English: For a nutritious home-made feed for local chickens (about 8-10 months old), mix roughly: 40% maize or sorghum, 27% bran, 20% oilseed cake (sesame, cotton, or groundnut), plus smaller amounts of fish meal, salt, and mineral premix. Chickens raised on natural feed (not commercial feed with medication) fetch better prices from consumers.
Kiswahili: Kwa chakula bora cha nyumbani kwa kuku wa asili (wenye umri wa miezi 8-10), changanya kwa uwiano huu: asilimia 40 mahindi au mtama, asilimia 27 pumba, asilimia 20 mashudu ya mafuta (ufuta, pamba, au karanga), pamoja na kiasi kidogo cha unga wa samaki, chumvi, na madini ya nyongeza. Kuku wanaolishwa chakula cha asili (si chakula cha kibiashara chenye dawa) huuzwa kwa bei nzuri zaidi.
Source: Farm Radio International, "Preparing feed for local chickens in agroecological ways" (scripts.farmradio.fm/radio-script/preparing-feed-for-local-chickens-in-agroecological-ways/), Dodoma Region, Tanzania
Metadata: tone=advisory; platform=Farm Radio International script; urgency=low; translation=team; source_lang=en; country=Tanzania

English: To store potatoes longer without them rotting or drying out, layer them with sawdust in a store (alternating layers of sawdust and potatoes, starting and ending with sawdust). The sawdust must be kept moist but not too wet - too dry and the potatoes shrivel and attract pests, too wet and they rot.
Kiswahili: Ili kuhifadhi viazi kwa muda mrefu bila kuoza au kukauka, weka tabaka za mbao (sawdust) kati ya viazi ghalani (tabaka za mbao na viazi zikibadilishana, ukianza na kumaliza na mbao). Mbao lazima ziwe na unyevu wa wastani - zikiwa kavu sana viazi hukauka na kushambuliwa na wadudu, zikiwa na maji mengi viazi huoza.
Source: Farm Radio International, "Sawdust prolongs the storage life of potatoes" (scripts.farmradio.fm/radio-script/sawdust-prolongs-the-storage-life-of-potatoes/), Kenya
Metadata: tone=advisory; platform=Farm Radio International script; urgency=low; translation=team; source_lang=en; country=Kenya

English: To protect stored maize from weevils without chemicals: once cobs are fully dry, remove the kernels, pound the empty cobs into a fine powder, mix this with the kernels, and pack tightly into jute sacks. The powder blocks the weevils' movement so they cannot find new kernels to infest, protecting the maize for up to 12 months.
Kiswahili: Ili kulinda mahindi yaliyohifadhiwa dhidi ya vidudu bila kutumia kemikali: mara vitumba vikiwa vimekauka kabisa, ondoa punje, twanga vitumba vitupu hadi kuwa unga laini, changanya unga huo na punje, kisha fungasha kwa nguvu kwenye magunia ya jute. Unga huo huzuia mwendo wa vidudu hivyo hushindwa kupata punje mpya za kushambulia, hivyo kuhifadhi mahindi hadi miezi 12.
Source: Farm Radio International, "Innovative farmer uses pounded maize cobs to protect stored maize" (scripts.farmradio.fm/radio-script/innovative-farmer-uses-pounded-maize-cobs-to-protect-stored-maize/), Benin
Metadata: tone=advisory; platform=Farm Radio International script; urgency=low; translation=team; source_lang=en; country=Benin

English: To control striga weed, pull it out by hand as soon as it starts flowering and before it produces new seeds; pull carefully so the stem doesn't break, then put the plants in a plastic bag and burn them immediately - do not leave them on the ground, as the tiny seeds will fall and spread. Combine hand-pulling with crop rotation and soil fertilization for better control.
Kiswahili: Ili kudhibiti gugu la striga, ling'oe kwa mkono mara linapoanza kuchanua maua na kabla halijazaa mbegu mpya; ling'oe kwa uangalifu ili shina lisikatike, kisha weka mimea kwenye mfuko wa plastiki na uichome mara moja - usiiache ardhini, kwani mbegu ndogo zitaanguka na kuenea. Changanya kung'oa kwa mkono na kubadilisha mazao na kurutubisha udongo kwa udhibiti bora zaidi.
Source: Farm Radio International, "Remove Striga Weeds Carefully from your Field" (scripts.farmradio.fm/radio-script/remove-striga-weeds-carefully-from-your-field/)
Metadata: tone=advisory; platform=Farm Radio International script; urgency=medium; translation=team; source_lang=en

English: To prevent coccidiosis and mycoplasmosis in poultry, cattle, sheep, and goats: raise feeding and watering troughs above the ground to stop contamination from droppings, and keep livestock sheds dry and clean, since humid, unhygienic conditions favour infection with both diseases.
Kiswahili: Ili kuzuia magonjwa ya koksidiosisi na mycoplasmosisi kwa kuku, ng'ombe, kondoo, na mbuzi: inua vyombo vya chakula na maji juu ya ardhi ili kuzuia uchafuzi kutoka kwa kinyesi, na weka mabanda ya mifugo yakiwa makavu na safi, kwani mazingira yenye unyevunyevu na uchafu huchochea maambukizi ya magonjwa yote mawili.
Source: Farm Radio International, "Managing livestock diseases: Mycoplasmosis and coccidiosis" (scripts.farmradio.fm/radio-script/managing-livestock-diseases-mycoplasmosis-and-coccidiosis/)
Metadata: tone=advisory; platform=Farm Radio International backgrounder; urgency=medium; translation=team; source_lang=en

English: If you use improved fallows (planting a cover crop/shrub to rest and restore land) to improve soil fertility, remember to replace the phosphorus removed when you cut the shrubs before you plant your next crop - add compost or manure, or for best results apply a phosphate fertilizer (such as DAP, SSP, TSP, or rock phosphate).
Kiswahili: Ukitumia mfumo wa kupumzisha ardhi kwa mazao au vichaka vya kufunika (improved fallows) ili kuboresha rutuba ya udongo, kumbuka kurejesha fosforasi iliyoondolewa wakati wa kukata vichaka kabla ya kupanda zao lako lijalo - ongeza mboji au samadi, au kwa matokeo bora tumia mbolea ya fosforasi (kama DAP, SSP, TSP, au fosforasi ya mwamba).
Source: Farm Radio International, "Farmers who use improved fallows must replace phosphorous in soils" (scripts.farmradio.fm/radio-script/farmers-who-use-improved-fallows-must-replace-phosphorous-in-soils/)
Metadata: tone=advisory; platform=Farm Radio International script; urgency=medium; translation=team; source_lang=en

English: As a free, locally-available pesticide for pests and diseases in beans, some farmers grind the leaves of Tephrosia vogelii (known locally by various names), soak them in water for several hours, filter the water, and spray it on both infected and healthy bean plants. Note this method hasn't been scientifically tested for safety, so use with care.
Kiswahili: Kama dawa ya wadudu ya bure na inayopatikana kienyeji kwa wadudu na magonjwa ya maharagwe, baadhi ya wakulima husaga majani ya Tephrosia vogelii (yanayojulikana kwa majina mbalimbali kienyeji), kuyaroweka majini kwa masaa kadhaa, kuchuja maji, na kunyunyizia kwenye mimea ya maharagwe iliyoathirika na yenye afya. Kumbuka njia hii haijafanyiwa utafiti wa kisayansi kuhusu usalama wake, hivyo itumike kwa tahadhari.
Source: Farm Radio International, "Women farmers use local methods to fight pests and diseases in beans" (scripts.farmradio.fm/radio-script/women-farmers-use-local-methods-to-fight-pests-and-diseases-in-beans/), Kigoma Region, Tanzania
Metadata: tone=advisory; platform=Farm Radio International script; urgency=low; translation=team; source_lang=en; country=Tanzania

English: Before planting, clear weeds and dig minimal-disturbance holes for seeds; while crops grow, use natural biopesticides first and chemical pesticides only for stubborn pests; add mulch, compost, and manure to boost soil fertility and retain moisture; and after harvest, rotate to an unrelated crop (for example, beans after maize) to improve soil health and reduce pests and diseases.
Kiswahili: Kabla ya kupanda, safisha magugu na chimba mashimo ya mbegu kwa kuvuruga udongo kidogo iwezekanavyo; wakati mazao yanakua, tumia dawa asilia za kuulia wadudu kwanza na tumia dawa za kemikali tu kwa wadudu wagumu kudhibiti; ongeza matandazo, mboji, na samadi kuboresha rutuba ya udongo na kuhifadhi unyevu; na baada ya mavuno, badilisha na zao tofauti (kwa mfano maharagwe baada ya mahindi) ili kuboresha afya ya udongo na kupunguza wadudu na magonjwa.
Source: Farm Radio International, "Radio spots on circular and regenerative agriculture", Spot #1 (scripts.farmradio.fm/radio-script/radio-spots-on-circular-and-regenerative-agriculture/), Uganda
Metadata: tone=advisory; platform=Farm Radio International radio spot; urgency=low; translation=team; source_lang=en; country=Uganda

English: To improve soil fertility and get a source of firewood, plant Gliricidia sepium trees (grown from seed or stem cuttings) in alley rows alongside your crops - space trees 100cm apart within rows, with 5 metres between rows, to allow enough sunlight and easy pruning and harvesting.
Kiswahili: Ili kuboresha rutuba ya udongo na kupata chanzo cha kuni, panda miti ya Gliricidia sepium (inayoweza kuoteshwa kutoka mbegu au vipandikizi vya shina) kwa mistari ya njia kando ya mazao yako - weka nafasi ya sentimita 100 kati ya miti ndani ya mstari, na mita 5 kati ya mistari, ili kuruhusu mwanga wa kutosha na urahisi wa kupogoa na kuvuna.
Source: Farm Radio International, "Plant Gliricidia sepium for soil fertility and fuelwood" (scripts.farmradio.fm/radio-script/plant-gliricidia-sepium-for-soil-fertility-and-fuelwood/), Eastern Province, Zambia
Metadata: tone=advisory; platform=Farm Radio International script; urgency=low; translation=team; source_lang=en; country=Zambia

English: During Uganda's May rains, farmers and communities are advised to monitor weather updates and early warnings, harvest rainwater to maximize agricultural production, secure roofs and structures before storms, and clear drainage channels to reduce flood damage to crops and property.
Kiswahili: Wakati wa mvua za Mei nchini Uganda, wakulima na jamii wanashauriwa kufuatilia taarifa za hali ya hewa na tahadhari za mapema, kuvuna maji ya mvua ili kuongeza uzalishaji wa kilimo, kuimarisha paa na miundo kabla ya dhoruba, na kusafisha mifereji ya maji ili kupunguza uharibifu wa mafuriko kwa mazao na mali.
Source: Uganda Ministry of Water and Environment, Weather Update for May 2026 (necoc.opm.go.ug/NRVA/May 2026 Monthly Weather Update.pdf), OCR-extracted, image-only PDF
Metadata: tone=advisory; platform=government meteorological bulletin; urgency=medium; translation=team; source_lang=en; country=Uganda

English: To prevent maize downy mildew disease (locally called 'nanzikambe' in Chichewa): till the field deeply before planting, use certified seed from licensed sellers, avoid planting maize near sugarcane, use recommended plant spacing for good airflow, rotate maize with legume crops, and treat seed with Metalaxyl fungicide (6g per kg of seed).
Kiswahili: Ili kuzuia ugonjwa wa ukungu wa mahindi (unaojulikana Malawi kama 'nanzikambe'): lima shamba kwa kina kabla ya kupanda, tumia mbegu zilizothibitishwa kutoka kwa wauzaji walioidhinishwa, epuka kupanda mahindi karibu na miwa, panda kwa nafasi inayopendekezwa ili hewa ipite vizuri, badilisha mahindi na mazao ya jamii ya mikunde, na tibu mbegu kwa dawa ya kuvu ya Metalaxyl (gramu 6 kwa kilo ya mbegu).
Source: Malawi Ministry of Agriculture, "Kuzindikira ndi kulimbana ndi matenda a nanzikambe mu chimanga" [Recognizing and fighting downy mildew disease in maize], dodma.gov.mw/newssingle/3
Metadata: tone=advisory; platform=government news/extension article; urgency=medium; translation=team; source_lang=ny; country=Malawi; note=translated from Chichewa (not English), a new source language for this project - recommend a native-speaker check before final submission

English: If your maize is infected with downy mildew disease: uproot and bury infected plants promptly, avoid walking through infected areas to prevent spreading the disease, remove volunteer sorghum shoots from the field, and after harvest burn or bury crop residues from affected fields; consult your nearest agricultural extension officer for more guidance.
Kiswahili: Ikiwa mahindi yako yameshambuliwa na ugonjwa wa ukungu (nanzikambe): ng'oa na uzike mimea iliyoathirika mara moja, epuka kutembea kwenye maeneo yaliyoathirika ili kuzuia kuenea kwa ugonjwa, ondoa machipukizi ya mtama yanayojitokeza yenyewe shambani, na baada ya mavuno choma au zika mabaki ya mazao kutoka mashamba yaliyoathirika; wasiliana na afisa ugani wa kilimo aliye karibu nawe kwa ushauri zaidi.
Source: Malawi Ministry of Agriculture, "Kuzindikira ndi kulimbana ndi matenda a nanzikambe mu chimanga" [Recognizing and fighting downy mildew disease in maize], dodma.gov.mw/newssingle/3
Metadata: tone=advisory; platform=government news/extension article; urgency=medium; translation=team; source_lang=ny; country=Malawi; note=translated from Chichewa (not English), a new source language for this project - recommend a native-speaker check before final submission

English: To avoid buying counterfeit maize seed, look for the scratch-code sticker on the seed packet, scratch it, and send the code to the toll-free verification number to confirm authenticity before planting - as KEPHIS Deputy Director for Seed Certification Ephraim Wachira put it, 'This sticker is what helps farmers distinguish between genuine and fake seed.'
